title: Human Translational Bioinformatics Core
text:
The overall objective of Center is to use a series of basic science experiments to understand how risk for
cardiometabolic diseases differs between men and women. The role of the Human Translational Bioinformatics
Core will be to serve as the hub for computational analyses that translate findings from the experimental projects
for association and relevance to cardiometabolic traits in humans. These cost-effective and efficient analyses
may, in turn, reveal additional biological information and lead to new hypotheses that can be investigated
experimentally.

title: Personalized Auricular Point Acupressure for Chronic Pain Self-Management in Rural Populations
text:
Chronic pain is a major health concern and places an enormous burden on society and healthcare systems in
the U.S., especially in rural areas. This project aims to plan and test auricular point acupressure self-
management (APA-SM) integrated into primary care. We will conduct a real-world trial to evaluate clinical
effectiveness, implementation outcomes, and cost-effectiveness toward revolutionizing pain management
particularly for rural populations.

title: Stromal Foxf2 suppresses prostate cancer progression
text:
The proposed studies will define novel mechanisms underlying aggressive features of human prostate cancer
and reveal novel stromal cell-mediated regulatory mechanisms in tumor microenvironment that can be
therapeutically exploited for the treatment of aggressive prostate cancer.

title: Mechanisms for building and remodeling microtubule arrays
text:
Protein polymers called microtubules are a critical part of the dynamic internal scaffolding of eukaryotic cells.
They have the remarkable ability to change their configuration to allow cells to accomplish such different tasks
as division, migration, transport of internal material and shape acquisition. Our research seeks to identify and
characterize the mechanisms underlying microtubule dynamics and spatial organization, which will contribute
to improving human health because defects in these mechanisms are linked to neurodegenerative diseases,
cancer, and developmental disorders.

title: Identification of Demographic, Clinical, and Genetic profiles for Suicidal Behavior in US Veterans
text:
This project aims to improve the identification of high-risk Veterans and decrease suicidal behavior through
enhanced and evidence-based screening methods and through individualized risk assessments based on
demographic, clinical, and genetic risk factors. Risk factors identified through this study would be important to
include as part of routine suicide prevention efforts, and the genetic risk factors identified through this study
could be incorporated into comprehensive medical treatment plans. If successful, early detection of Veterans at
greater risk for suicidal behavior will allow for early intervention and lower rates of suicide attempt and death.

title: Quantitative Fluorescence Imaging-Guided Detection and Targeted Therapy Monitoring Platform for Ovarian Cancer Micrometastases
text:
A quantitative laparoscopic spatial frequency domain imaging platform is proposed to map intraperitoneal
ovarian metastases as well as to treat them effectively via targeted chemo-photo therapy. Cancer-targeting
drug and optimized light delivery will allow local release and preferential uptake of the drug into tumors versus
normal tissue for optimal cancer cell destruction with minimal side effects to the surrounding normal tissue.
This approach is relevant to public health as it is expected to significantly improve detection and destruction of
micromets in ovarian cancer patients, and reduce side effects in normal tissue, thereby fulfilling the
overarching goal of improving patients’ survival rates and quality of life.

title: Imaging and multi-omics analyses to identify molecular subtypes of distinct emphysema patterns
text:
Emphysema is one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and there are currently no
treatments available to reverse the resulting lung damage. This study aims to find new biomarkers that can
predict the early onset of emphysema, distinguish between its diverse pathologic patterns and their regional
distributions, and provide insights into the underlying pathobiology. A better understanding of emphysema and
its subtypes will aid in the development of novel and personalized therapies to improve the health of millions of
affected individuals.

title: Computer-Vision and Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis Pipeline to Improve Diagnosis in Pediatric Subglottic Stenosis
text:
Pediatric subglottic stenosis (SGS) is a common disorder that is challenging to diagnose due to a varying
clinical spectrum and major limitations in the gold-standard severity grading scale. In this proposal we
demonstrate a novel diagnostic pipeline that combines engineering analysis and computer vision algorithms to
provide personalized and objective diagnostic measures of stenosed airway physiology. The analysis pipeline
is widely adoptable, provides novel precision metrics to guide patient management, and thus has the potential
to transform the clinical care of this sensitive population.

title: A deep learning artifact removal method for CPR continuity throughout the shock decision in AEDs
text:
Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) affects more than 475,000 people in the United States each
year. Major determinants of survival from OHCA include continuous high quality
cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) coupled with timely defibrillatory shock, if warranted,
based on accurate shock decisions. Since CPR introduces severe motion artifacts into the ECG,
automated external defibrillators require cessation of CPR for up to 20 seconds to determine
whether an arrhythmia is shockable or non-shockable. The current work proposes to remove CPR
artifacts in near real-time without CPR stoppage so that accurate shock decisions can be made.

title: Leveraging Novel Randomized Clinical Trials of Vitamin D Supplementation in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: Impact on Survival and Anti-Tumor Immunity
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because colorectal cancer is the second leading cause of
cancer death in the U.S., and new treatment strategies are urgently needed. Abundant preclinical and epidemi-
ologic data link lower levels of circulating vitamin D to increased risk of and mortality from colorectal cancer, but
causal evidence from randomized clinical trials is needed before vitamin D supplementation can be incorporated
into standard of care treatment. This proposal will provide causal evidence in support of the clinical efficacy of
vitamin D supplementation in patients with colorectal cancer, as well as elucidate underlying mechanisms of
action on the immune tumor microenvironment that may lead to novel combination treatment strategies with
immunotherapy agents.

title: REGULATION OF CAPILLARY HEMODYNAMICS BY THIN-STRANDED PERICYTES
text:
As the smallest vessels in the circulatory system, capillaries networks, which are made up of endothelial cells
and pericytes, are the sites of gas and nutrient exchange between the vasculature and surrounding neurons of
the brain. With three morphologically-distinct subtypes of pericytes, the current proposal aims to study a novel
role for thin-stranded pericytes in neurovascular coupling, a process linking fluctuations in neural activity with
changes in the directed delivery of O2 and nutrients. Completion of the proposal will provide insights into the
active role capillaries play in ensuring that O2 is delivered to active neurons and possibly uncover new
molecular targets for therapeutic intervention for cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Stroke Connectome MRI Biomarkers for VCID Risk Assessment
text:
Every year more than 795,000 people in the United States have a stroke with currently around 4.7 million stroke
survivors, and approximately 20% of the survivors go on to develop cognitive impairments and dementia later in
life. This research project will seek an improved basic scientific understanding of the how the complex biological
interactions between vascular and demographic risk factors (e.g., disadvantaged neighborhoods), baseline brain
and cognitive health, and adaptive or maladaptive brain changes following an ischemic stroke, underlie the
biology of vascular contributions to cognitive impairments and dementia (VCID). It will also seek development of
diagnostic and prognostic tools based on non-invasive high-quality MRI biomarkers which may aid in positively
altering disease progression and reducing the burden of illness on patients due to post ischemic stroke VCID.

title: Rationally Designed, Target-specific Imaging Probes for Nephro-urology Diagnoses
text:
Following a recombinant design approach, we will develop and characterize a series of kidney-
specific radionuclide imaging probes for targeting the structures and functions of the kidney. The
proposed studies are designed to accomplish our research goal of assessing renal
pathophysiology in diseases in a minimally invasive fashion with molecular specificity.

title: Role of CCN6 (WISP3) in the progression and metastasis of breast cancer
text:
Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) and its aggressive subtype, metaplastic carcinoma (mBrCA), have high
metastatic potential and no effective therapeutics. This grant will address a novel mechanism of breast cancer
metastasis by investigating how CCN6 regulates mitochondrial metabolism and cell differentiation. Our studies,
including work with unique tissue samples, may discover prognostic and diagnostic biomarkers of metastasis.

title: Aptamers as Novel Inhibitors of the Neurotoxin Beta-methylamino-L-alanine (BMAA)
text:
The role of the biotoxin BMAA in promoting human disease will be investigated by establishing its functional
effects in several human cell lines using a combination of gene expression and functional assays. Novel
aptamers targeting BMAA will be generated and tested in cell culture models for their potential in inhibiting
BMAA functions.

title: INRSA Training Grant in Gastroenterology
text:
This application is for support of three training positions in an established program in digestive diseases that
has been funded since 1975 at the Division of Gastroenterology, University of California, San Francisco. The
Program’s goal is to prepare trainees for careers in academic luminal gastroenterology. These talented
individuals are well poised to capitalize on the exciting state of GI related research, with its transformative and
translational potential.

title: Ultrafine Particle Generator and Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer Integrated System
text:
This proposal seeks support for the purchase of a new integrated system that is comprised of ultrafine particle
aerosol generation and characterization with added safety and monitoring features that will be used in an
Inhalation Exposure Facility (IEF) at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry to replace
aging and heavily-used existing equipment. The Rochester IEF is unique in its focus on ultrafine particles, which
are components of traffic-related ambient air pollution that have been implicated in adverse health outcomes in
the pulmonary, cardiovascular, and central nervous systems. The translational basic science supportive
infrastructure of the IEF for ultrafine particle exposures is used in several current projects that are funded by NIH
and other agencies, so modernization and replacement of this equipment is urgent and critical to the successful
completion of these projects.

title: SHP2 Signaling from Molecule to Mouse
text:
Relevance: SHP2 is a canonical member of the RAS/ERK cascade essential for SOS/RAS activation, a key
developmental disease and oncogene, and a major drug target, yet much about its mechanism of action,
physiological, and pathological roles remains unknown. Our work will reveal how SHP2 regulates RAS activation
and clarify the role of its sub-domains in vitro, in normal/pathological mouse development, and in oncogenesis.
The results should have important implications for normal human biology, shed new light on the pathogenesis of
major developmental disorders and neoplasia, and suggest novel approaches to SHP2-targeted therapeutics.

title: Etiology and Tumor Characteristics of Early-onset Pancreatic Cancer
text:
The rising incidence of pancreatic cancer among younger populations in the United States and the lack of
knowledge regarding the etiology and tumor characteristics of early-onset pancreatic cancer highlight the need
for further investigation. This proposal aims to identify modifiable factors associated with the development of
early-onset pancreatic cancer and characterize the clinicopathologic and molecular features of tumors in affected
patients. The findings from this study will contribute to improved disease prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Discovery of Pathways and Molecular Mediators of Early T1D Pathogenesis using Spatial Multi-Omics
text:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a devastating disease that we still know very little about the molecular mechanisms of
the disease development and progression. Herein, we propose to identify novel in situ pathways and molecular
mediators during the preclinical phase of type 1 diabetes by spatial omics profiling of human islet
microenvironments within patient pancreatic tissue samples. Novel mediators identified from this high-
dimensional dataset will be further assessed for their functional and translational significance as potential
therapeutic targets.
